prompt: A frame from a 35mm feature film, full-bleed: Chicago, 1928, a cold dry night in a small town square of trampled frost and cinder grit, the iron girders of the elevated railway cutting across the top of the frame. We look from low behind the bandstand rail, a peeling green rail and a dented brass music stand in the near foreground, past the mayor's shoulder: a tall, skinny man in a bowler hat with a heavy gold chain of office round his neck, a long narrow face, hollow cheeks, a pencil-thin grey moustache, one arm flung up as a tray of flash powder bursts in his hand. The burst is the only light. It throws billowing clouds of chemical smoke, strontium crimson boiling into copper blue-green and sodium yellow, lit from inside so the colour rolls over a hundred upturned faces in flat caps and headscarves, mouths open. Through a torn gap in the coloured smoke, off to the right and far back, a dusty black Packard sedan lurches away from the granite bank steps, rear wheels spitting grit, a tommy gun barrel poking up at the sky from its back window. The frame tilts a few degrees. Everything outside the smoke falls to deep black. All signs and paper stay blank, no lettering.
